1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3.strategy: The flexible main move: it defends e4 and develops a piece while White still decides how to build the rest of the centre. The cost is the c3 square, so the c-pawn can no longer blunt Black's fianchettoed bishop. Black has to undermine the broad centre from the flanks.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3.name: Modern Defence: Standard Line

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.c4.strategy: Adds a third central pawn for the largest space advantage on offer. The big front needs pieces behind it: d4 is guarded only by the queen for now, so White must develop with care or the pawns become targets for the bishop on g7.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3.strategy: A quiet developing move that guards d4 with a piece, so Black's bishop has nothing to bite on, and keeps the pawn structure undecided. Many lines transpose into the other set-ups, so White chooses the type of game later.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bc4.strategy: Develops with an eye on f7 and controls d5, but commits the bishop before the knights are out, and e4 has no piece defending it. Black can treat the bishop as a target and gain time while completing development.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bc4.name: Modern Defence: Bishop Attack

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.f4.strategy: Builds a huge pawn centre, ready to gain more space with e5, but commits the f-pawn before a piece is out and weakens White's own king side. Black's bishop and a quick strike with the c-pawn hit d4 at once, so the pawns can become targets.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.f4.name: Modern Defence: Three Pawns Attack

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3.strategy: Mirrors Black's fianchetto and prepares a bishop that covers e4 and the long diagonal. But it is slow: d4 is guarded only by the queen and e4 stands unprotected for now, so Black strikes at the centre at once.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bd2.strategy: Blocks the queen's protection of d4, so Black simply takes the pawn with the bishop and is a clean pawn up. White hopes for quick development in return, but a pawn for a few tempi is a poor price.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bd2.name: Modern Defence: Westermann Gambit

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bd3.strategy: Blocks the queen from d4 as well: Black takes the pawn with the bishop. The bishop does keep e4 protected, but it gets in the way of the d-pawn's support and nothing here pays for the lost pawn.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bd3.name: Modern Defence: Wind Gambit

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6.strategy: The standard move: it controls e5, opens the c8 bishop and prepares to develop the knight to f6. Black accepts White's centre and plans to attack it from the flanks and with pieces, keeping a flexible and solid set-up.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c6.strategy: A solid way to prepare a central challenge without committing a piece: the pawn supports a coming ...d5 and keeps the g7 bishop's diagonal open. The cost is time, since only one piece is developed and White can build a broad centre at leisure.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 c5.strategy: Strikes at d4 with a pawn and leaves the centre to White, relying on queenside activity and pressure on the c3 knight. It is a sharp, rarely played idea: Black gets counterplay quickly, but White's centre and space are real.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 b6.strategy: Prepares a second fianchetto, so both bishops aim down the long diagonals at White's centre. It leaves that centre untouched and costs time, so White can expand freely while Black waits for a target.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 b6.name: Modern Defence: Mongredien Defence, with Nc3

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d5.strategy: Offers the pawn at once. After exd5 Black cannot take it back: ...Qxd5 loses the queen to the knight and ...Bxd4 loses the bishop to the queen. White is simply a pawn up and keeps the centre.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d5.name: Modern Defence: Lizard Defence, Mittenberger Gambit

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bc4 b5.strategy: A gambit to gain time against the bishop. After Bxb5 White has won a pawn, and Black has only some play on the half-open b-file in return, with the g7 bishop and quick development to count on.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bc4 b5.name: Modern Defence: Bishop Attack, Bücker Gambit

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.f4 c5.strategy: Hits d4 at once with the pawn and the bishop, before White's centre is backed by pieces. Black fights for the centre where it is weakest, and White's loosened king side stays a long-term factor.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5.strategy: Attacks d4 twice, with the pawn and the bishop, while it is guarded only by the queen. White must defend or resolve the tension at once, and the fianchetto has not yet had time to cover the centre.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3 d6.strategy: The standard set-up: the pawn controls e5 and gives the g7 bishop a free diagonal, so the knight can later come to f6 without being kicked by e5. Black attacks the centre from a distance instead of occupying it.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3 c5.strategy: Strikes at d4 at once. If White takes, ...Qa5+ and ...Qxc5 usually regain the pawn; if White holds the centre, Black has queenside space and the g7 bishop for counterplay. A direct way to challenge the pawn centre.

1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3 b6.strategy: Prepares a second fianchetto, so that both bishops aim at the centre along the long diagonals. It costs time and gives White room to develop and expand, and the queenside pawns become a little loose.
1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nf3 b6.name: Modern Defence: Mongredien Defence, with Nf3
